jobs.title: What it's called
jobs.prompt: a four-panel newspaper comic strip, four equal panels in a single horizontal row with thin black gutters (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, the same faces, hair and builds in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 19, thin young man with a slouch, three days' stubble, dark hair grown longer; THE PRINT TECH — wiry man of forty with a gray crew cut and ink under his nails, a dry half-smile, leans on the copier like it's his. Clothes, hair-dos and anything held come from this strip's description, never from the reference sheet; hands are empty unless a panel names what they hold. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: The print tech asks what the digest is called. It's called the digest. He means the strip. The strip is called Drift Wood. He asks why. Wood has never been asked. Panel 1: a print shop technician in an apron holding a comic strip up to the light while a young man waits beside a large photocopier, black and white, no words (in this panel: WOOD, THE PRINT TECH). Tech says "What's it called.". Wood says "The digest.". Tech says "Not the booklet. This.". Panel 2: a young man's face caught off guard, mouth slightly open, black and white, no words. Wood says "Drift Wood.". Tech says "Why.". Panel 3: a young man watching the green light of a photocopier sweep under its lid, thinking, black and white, no words. No dialogue in this panel. Panel 4: a technician stacking warm photocopies while a young man answers, black and white, no words. Wood says "It's what washes up.". Tech says "Huh. Thought it was your name.". Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @dw_2001_10_09_lot_c is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Match the attached references: @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23; @dw_2001_10_09_lot_c for a finished strip in this style; @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17.
